title: Multilingual Museum Audio Guide Personalization
business: A global museum network providing inclusive audio tours for international visitors.
problem: The museum struggles with high production costs and long lead times for recording professional voice actors in 17 different languages for every new exhibit.
solution: By utilizing XTTS-v2, the museum can generate high-quality, localized audio guides using a single 6-second reference clip from a primary narrator, ensuring consistent voice identity across all supported languages.
steps: Select a professional narrator to record a 6-second reference audio clip.
Upload the reference clip to the XTTS-v2 inference environment.
Input the exhibit description text and specify the target language code.
Execute the synthesis process to generate the localized audio file.
Review the output for prosody and clarity before deploying to the mobile guide application.
outcome: The museum achieves a seamless, personalized visitor experience where the narrator's voice remains consistent regardless of the language selected by the guest.
limitation: The model may exhibit varying degrees of prosodic accuracy across different languages; developers should verify output quality by listening to generated samples to ensure the emotional tone matches the exhibit content.

diagram.description: This diagram illustrates the transformation of source text into localized audio using a reference voice.

code.content:
from TTS.api import TTS
# Initialize the multilingual model
tts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2", gpu=True)
# Generate localized audio using a narrator reference clip
tts.tts_to_file(text="Welcome to the exhibit.", file_path="output.wav", speaker_wav="narrator_ref.wav", language="fr")
